children: , the social-media and digital-advertising giant, unveiled Muse, a personal AI agent designed to handle real-world tasks through third-party applications. Shares jumped approximately 6.6% to $653.61 Wednesday morning, signaling that investors see a more direct path from Meta's massive AI spending to consumer revenue.

Muse can write and send emails, arrange travel, fill out forms and make purchases once users grant permission. The agent runs inside a dedicated virtual machine and will initially reach consumers through its standalone application and WhatsApp. Reuters reported that Meta plans to combine free access with subscription tiers priced at $20 and $100 per month.

The valuation picture adds fuel to the rally. The chart places Meta's GF Value at $849.92, leaving the $653.61 share price 23.1% below that estimate. Still, monetizing Muse at meaningful scale will take more than Meta's 3.6 billion daily users: even 10 million customers paying $20 monthly would generate $2.4 billion annually, or only about 1% of the company's current annualized revenue base. Muse has enormous distribution, but trust and repeat usage will decide whether it becomes a serious second engine beyond advertising.

title: Meta Soars 6.6% as Muse Turns WhatsApp Into an AI Operator
